Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 5, 2026, 7:02 AM ET / 11:02 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Makes database compatibility checks asynchronous and ties startup snapshot workers to Gateway cancellation and cleanup, while preserving Update and Doctor sequencing. > [!WARNING] > **SQLite table change** > > This PR modifies persisted SQLite tables in `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts`. Prefer a design that avoids changing persisted SQLite tables. If the change is necessary, verify migration and upgrade compatibility against an existing database before merge. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 3 items remain** Still useful: current main retains blocking schema snapshots. No concrete introduced correctness defect found; the declared final Linux lifecycle verification remains outstanding. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Coherent ownership repair with meaningful regression coverage and no identified correctness defect; final compiled lifecycle verification remains a material risk reducer. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The maintainer-authored PR is exempt from the ordinary contributor-proof gate; reported live-WAL and child-close results support the snapshot owner, while final compiled Linux Gateway startup-stage cancellation remains explicitly pending. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The maintainer-authored PR is exempt from the ordinary contributor-proof gate; reported live-WAL and child-close results support the snapshot owner, while final compiled Linux Gateway startup-stage cancellation remains explicitly pending. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Current main still needs the fix: Fetched main imports and calls prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationSync for both state and agent schema inspection. The proposed asynchronous behavior is therefore still distinct.
Startup ownership boundary: Both ownership inspection and schema preflight receive the per-start operation callback. Accepted stops close admission and drain that scope before server close; cancellation is joined through the retained stop completion.
Snapshot transport and dependency boundary: The worker runs the existing OpenClaw SQLite entrypoint with process.execPath, waits for child close, and lets the snapshot owner remove parent-owned staging. Schema inspection retains the byte-preserving copy strategy. This path depends on Node child-process behavior, with no affirmative Codex dependency signal. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Before Gateway startup, updates, and Doctor maintenance, OpenClaw inspects existing SQLite databases for compatibility. Private snapshot workers feed those checks; the Gateway host now owns their cancellation and cleanup during startup. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway startup or maintenance] --> B[Database preflight] C[Existing SQLite stores] --> D[Private snapshot worker] B --> D D --> E[Version and shape checks] E --> F[Continue or report refusal] G[Gateway stop request] --> H[Cancel worker and join cleanup] H --> D ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Final compiled Linux verification remains pending for stopping during ownership inspection and schema preflight; composed process exit, worker teardown, and staging cleanup are not yet demonstrated for the final revision. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Attach final compiled Linux readiness and cancellation results for both startup database stages, plus the declared POSIX-lock verification. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.
Agent review details ### Security None. ### PR surface Source +186, Tests +466. Total +652 across 26 files.
View PR surface stats | Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Source | 16 | 333 | 147 | +186 | | Tests | 10 | 592 | 126 | +466 | | Docs | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Config | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Generated | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Other | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | **Total** | **26** | **925** | **273** | **+652** |
### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test growth** | Production net +186; tests net +466 | Transport moves cancel in the net; production growth supplies startup lifetime ownership and parent-owned staging, justified by the recorded orphan-worker failure. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `serialized state: src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts`, `unknown-data-model-change: src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Complete the declared Linux verification (recommended)** Attach the final compiled startup and stop results, including worker disappearance, staging cleanup, and POSIX-lock preservation. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the existing isolated snapshot strategy under one host-owned cancellation and cleanup boundary, with compiled startup and shutdown behavior verified. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: current main synchronously waits for snapshot workers during schema inspection, and the existing live-WAL fixture supplies a focused event-loop regression path. This review did not execute it. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes, architecturally: reusing the snapshot owner and AsyncWorkScope addresses both blocking and worker lifetime; changing transport alone would leave the recorded orphan-worker failure unresolved. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Accepted stops close admission and drain that scope before server close; cancellation is joined through the retained stop completion. ([`src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts:881`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162/src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts#L881), [1ce6848dbbe3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162)) - **Snapshot transport and dependency boundary:** The worker runs the existing OpenClaw SQLite entrypoint with process.execPath, waits for child close, and lets the snapshot owner remove parent-owned staging. Schema inspection retains the byte-preserving copy strategy. This path depends on Node child-process behavior, with no affirmative Codex dependency signal. ([`src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts:83`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162/src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts#L83), [1ce6848dbbe3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162)) - **Direct child-process contract inspection:** Inspected the installed official Node v24.20.0 builtin source: abort can invoke the error callback before process close, while execFile registers its close callback before returning the child. The distribution README identifies nodejs/node; no dependency commit SHA was established. (`lib/child_process.js:521`) - **Sibling sequencing and stale recovery:** Package and Git mutation paths await preflight before beginMutation; interrupted or completed Windows recovery rejects there. Doctor awaits compatibility and final readiness checks, and managed reload already returns the readiness promise. ([`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-execution.ts:255`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-execution.ts#L255), [1ce6848dbbe3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162)) - **Regression coverage inspected:** The live-WAL test checks event-loop progress alongside committed versions and unchanged source artifacts. Cancellation coverage holds a real child after SIGTERM and requires close plus staging removal before settlement; run-loop tests cover queued restart followed by stop, duplicate signals, cleanup failure, and retained callbacks. ([`src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.artifacts.test.ts:107`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162/src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.artifacts.test.ts#L107), [1ce6848dbbe3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce6848dbbe3fbb83f91dadded8704ee517a5162)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 0d830e9e74488c1ee5a3af461b147cb683f0581f adds src/shared/async-work-scope.ts:32 relative to its recorded parents. On matched Linux / Node 26.7 compiled builds, baseline schema preflight serviced zero callbacks over 185.4 ms; the candidate serviced 33 over 169.4 ms, with a 5.41 ms largest adjacent in-phase gap. Both reached an owned readiness endpoint. This establishes preflight scheduling progress; it does not establish an overall startup-speed improvement.

Both real Gateway startup stop paths passed. During schema copying, the worker closed from SIGTERM in 7.15 ms and the parent closed with code 0 in 28.84 ms, with no later network bootstrap. During ownership inspection, the parent remained alive after accepted STOP while the exact child was deliberately paused; after the timing control was released, actual child SIGTERM close and staging cleanup preceded parent exit 0. No fallback signals, orphan workers, live group, or staging residue were needed to make either result pass.

All 32 changed checks and 772 focused tests passed; one Windows-only case was skipped on Linux. Live-WAL POSIX-lock and uncommitted-writer-version assertions passed explicitly. The independent baseline used its own checkout and frozen dependency install. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33961644334).
